clue.text: Be serious in prosecuting shabby affair?

definitions.meaning: to be determined and in earnest when pursuing something
a mean (shabby, stingy) piece of business, the question mark flagging the whimsical reading

explanation.surface: A lawyer weighs whether a sordid little affair deserves serious prosecution.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being in earnest also reads literally as a shabby or stingy affair.

clue.text: Battle in the shade means mother goes without

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for mother goes round the outside

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother
an agent is a means or instrument by which something is done

explanation.surface: Someone fights in the shade while mother goes without, as if in a hard-luck story.
explanation.walkthrough: Magenta was an 1859 battle in Italy, and the purplish-red dye discovered that year was named after it, so the battle is 'in the shade'.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour was named after the battle fought at that Italian town, so the battle lives on in a shade.

clue.text: Drawing this number's right in the ship

indicators.note: the number and the right-hand letter go inside the word for the ship

parts.note: the ark is Noah's ship
this clue is numbered two, so 'this number' is that word; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A drawing of a ship is described with a number and a right turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'number's' is 'is'. 'This number' refers to the clue's own number, 2.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing is a piece of illustrative work, a synonym in the sense of pictures prepared for print.

clue.text: A futile but abbreviated setting for the fair

indicators.note: a setting is an arrangement, so these letters are arranged afresh
the word but is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Something futile and shortened is placed in a setting for the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abbreviated' trims BUT to BU; with A FUTILE that gives nine letters for 'setting' to rearrange. 'for the' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in its old sense means lovely to look at, a synonym for good-looking.

clue.text: Opening of shopping precinct is 3

definitions.note: the answer at 3 completes the saying from Schumacher's book title about size and beauty

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of shopping

parts.note: a shopping precinct is a mall, and precinct alone supplies it here

explanation.surface: The opening of a shopping precinct is described as a lovely event.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the slogan 'Small is beautiful', the title of E. F. Schumacher's 1973 book: the answer followed by 'is 3' makes the saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Schumacher's slogan pairs this word with lovely, so the answer is the one that 'is beautiful'.

clue.text: Bouquet for patient fellow's work on hooter

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its nose, its smell
Job is the biblical figure famed for patience; the 's links to the work that follows

explanation.surface: A patient man is given flowers as he works on his car horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' is British slang for the nose; 'for' links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery to reshape the nose is work on the hooter, a slang word for the nose.

clue.text: Sun's exposure breaches the privacy of physical gratification

indicators.note: the scrambled star breaks into the word for privacy, splitting it

parts.note: a seal keeps something private, so it stands for privacy

indicators.note: being exposed jumbles the letters of sun into a new order

parts.note: the star's name, the 's a possessive

explanation.surface: A tabloid exposure breaches someone's privacy over their bodily pleasures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposure' is an unusual anagram signal: the star's letters laid open and jumbled. The Sun is also a British tabloid, which makes the privacy surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensual means relating to bodily pleasure, so it describes physical gratification.

clue.text: BAC SID SID SID … ?

parts.note: one word for the rear cut short, then several words for flanks each cut short, and an ellipsis

explanation.walkthrough: BAC is BACK cut short, SID is SIDE cut short and there are several of them, so the picture shows a short back and short sides. It is a classic British men's haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: The picture literally shows a back and some sides all cut short, like the barber's trim of that name.

clue.text: Meal named by English article

parts.note: hight is an archaic word meaning called or named
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A meal is given a name by an English article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' links the wordplay to the definition. HIGH TEA is a British early-evening cooked meal with tea.
explanation.definitionFit: This British early-evening meal, usually cooked and served with tea, is a type of meal.

clue.text: Most of 14 top people I caught using poison

indicators.note: all but the last part of the football club's name is used

parts.note: Arsenal, a top London football club, is a team of people at the top of the game named at 14
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Top people are caught using poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is FOOTBALLS, so '14 top people' is a top football side: Arsenal, a leading London club. 'Most of' drops AL; 'using' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The element is a notorious poison, long associated with murder mysteries.

clue.text: Sees war chest spent on nibbles

indicators.note: something spent is used up and broken, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sees a war chest frittered away on snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: These are cheesy pastry sticks, a type of savoury snack served as nibbles.

clue.text: Something to do with the old (drummer take note)

definitions.text: Something to do with the old

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer
ut is the old name for the note now called do

explanation.surface: An old drummer is told to take note of something about the past.
explanation.walkthrough: From Tennyson's 'Ring out the old, ring in the new'. 'take' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's line says to ring out the old year, so this is what one does with the old.

clue.text: The young French former film critic has shelter and month overlapping

definitions.text: The young French former film critic

indicators.note: the two words overlap, the month's first letter slipping back between the letters of the shelter word

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind; June is a month

explanation.surface: A young French film critic of the past has a shelter and a month that overlap.
explanation.walkthrough: C. A. Lejeune was film critic of The Observer for decades; her name is French for 'the young'. LEE and JUNE overlap with J slid between the Es.
explanation.definitionFit: Caroline Lejeune was a noted British film critic, and her surname is French for the young one.

clue.text: Bad mark is creditable and 3

definitions.meaning: a ... mark is a bad mark against one's name
an account in the ... is in credit
the slogan from the 1960s civil-rights era pairs this colour with lovely

explanation.surface: A bad mark is described as both creditable and lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: black mark, in the black, and the slogan 'Black is beautiful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense is a phrase with the colour: a black mark, being in the black, and the civil-rights slogan.

clue.text: Past and maybe future Labour MPs used in 3 game

parts.words: Past and maybe future Labour MPs
parts.note: Michael Foot was a past Labour leader

parts.words: Past and maybe future Labour MPs
parts.note: Ed Balls was a rising Labour MP, perhaps a future leader

explanation.surface: Labour MPs past and future are used in a lovely game.
explanation.walkthrough: Football is 'the beautiful game', so things used in it are footballs.
explanation.definitionFit: Football is called the beautiful game, and the balls kicked about in it are used in that game.

clue.text: Order flowers for chap who is a checker

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
buds are flowers yet to open
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Someone orders flowers for a man who checks things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'who is a' link the pieces and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman checks complaints against public bodies, so is an official checker.

clue.text: Game association with only men on the boards

definitions.text: Game association with only men on the boards

parts.words: Game association with only men on the boards
parts.note: an all-male stage company, or a society whose men are pieces on the boards of a board game

explanation.surface: A theatre group has only men acting on the boards.
explanation.definitionFit: A club for this board game has chessmen as its only men, standing on boards.

clue.text: African city where rising speculation has been twisted around

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes around the reversed bet
twisted letters are out of their usual order
in a down clue, rising means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a bet is a speculation

explanation.surface: In an African city rising speculation has been twisted around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' suits a down clue, where the word reads upwards. 'where' and 'has' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Entebbe is a city in Uganda on Lake Victoria, home to its main airport.

clue.text: Loudspeaker on Gun Hill

parts.note: a Sten is a British submachine gun
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A loudspeaker is set up on Gun Hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Stentor is the loud-voiced herald of the Iliad. 'on' joins the pieces in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentor was a Greek herald with a voice as loud as fifty men, hence any loud speaker.

clue.text: See 7
Guide holding a student is a thief

indicators.note: the guide word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to steer is to guide
L is for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A guide holding a student turns out to be a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A stealer is one who steals, synonymous with a thief.

clue.text: Hooker to leave shortly, retaining muck

indicators.note: the short form keeps the muck word inside it

parts.note: dep is the abbreviation for depart, to leave
mire is mud or muck

explanation.surface: A hooker is about to leave, still covered in muck.
explanation.definitionFit: A demirep is an old word for a woman of doubtful reputation, a prostitute.

clue.text: Woman on the boards gets a bit of salad — about time!

indicators.note: the salad leaf goes about the time letter

parts.note: cress is a salad leaf

explanation.surface: A woman gets a piece of salad at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the boards' is the stage. 'gets' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who performs on stage is a female actor, the boards being the stage.

clue.text: Clothing relating to singular 14? Remove it

definitions.meaning: a team's kit worn in football

explanation.surface: A football kit is mentioned, then told to come off.
explanation.definitionFit: A team's kit is called its strip, and to strip is to take off clothing.

clue.text: King of America, 3 in song

definitions.meaning: Martin Luther King, who said he had a dream

explanation.surface: An American king is lovely in a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther King voiced a dream for America, and Foster's song addresses a lovely one who dreams.

clue.text: I argue that mammal should eat mammal

indicators.note: eating takes the second animal inside the first

parts.note: a deer is a mammal
a bat is a mammal

explanation.surface: Someone argues that one mammal should eat another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: One who argues formally is a debater, so 'I argue' is what one would say.

clue.text: Grumpy Victor was an artist after honey

indicators.note: the drawing word comes after the honey word

parts.note: mel is Latin for honey, common in crosswords
drew means made pictures, as an artist does

explanation.surface: A grumpy man was an artist after some honey.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor Meldrew is the grumpy pensioner of the BBC sitcom One Foot in the Grave.
explanation.definitionFit: The famously grumpy pensioner of a BBC sitcom was named Victor Meldrew.

clue.text: Leader embracing endless looting gets endless hanging and you can tell no-one's making a row

definitions.text: you can tell no-one's making a row

indicators.note: the leader word embraces the shortened looting word

parts.note: a head is a leader

indicators.note: endless takes the last letter off the looting word

parts.note: rapine is plundering or looting

indicators.note: endless takes the last letter off the hanging word

parts.note: a rope is used for hanging

explanation.surface: A leader in the middle of looting faces the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'endless' indicators clip a final E. The definition is the idiom for silence so complete a falling pin could be heard; 'gets' and 'and' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: When it is so quiet that a tiny pin falling is audible, nobody is making any noise.
